long_biography.plain_text:
Michael Hintze studied physics, pure mathematics and electrical engineering in Sydney before serving as an Australian Army officer and working as a design engineer. An MBA led to fixed-income trading in New York and senior credit and markets roles at Goldman Sachs and Credit Suisse First Boston. He founded CQS in 1999, combining ownership of the firm with direct management of its Directional Opportunities strategy.

Manulife acquired the CQS institutional credit platform and brand in 2024, but not Hintze's retained fund. He transferred that strategy to Deltroit Asset Management, a firm he founded and controls. Deltroit manages investment funds containing both personal and other investor capital, so its assets under management are not his personal fortune. His disclosed portfolio also includes agriculture, property, aviation and private-company interests, while investment management remains his central current activity.

uncertainties.detail: Hintze retains his knighthood, but a life peer is ordinarily styled Lord Hintze. The proposed display and title fields therefore use Lord Michael Hintze and Lord, matching current Parliament, University and Companies House records rather than the superseded Sir Michael Hintze display.

No authoritative source reviewed gives a middle name. AM and other honours are post-nominals, not middle names or name suffixes in this schema, so the blank middle-name and suffix fields are not populated.

CQS and Deltroit manage capital for funds, mandates and investors. The dossier does not count CQS's former institutional assets or Deltroit's total managed assets as Hintze's personal wealth; only reliable statements about a personal-capital component and disclosed owned interests inform the relationship assessment.

Deltroit is a regulated investment manager rather than a purely private holding company and manages outside investor money as well as a substantial amount of Hintze's own capital. Family office principal is used for his post-CQS role because he founded, controls and actively directs the platform around retained and personal investments; it does not imply that every Deltroit fund asset belongs to him or his family.

The parliamentary register identifies interests across agriculture, property, aviation, technology, mining, energy, healthcare and private funds. Finance & Investments remains the primary classification because Deltroit is his current remunerated occupation and central controlled platform; the register supplies no values showing another sector predominates.

The source biography embeds external links, uses the superseded Sir style and places the Directional Opportunities Fund inside current CQS. Manulife's acquisition materials establish that the fund was excluded from the sale and transferred to Hintze's new platform, so replacement is proposed.

The existing Wikipedia URL redirects to the current Baron Hintze page. No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, Facebook, X, YouTube or TikTok profile was verified; the dedicated Forbes profile and official Deltroit site are proposed instead.

Politics, political donations, controversies, allegations, litigation, legal matters, private-family trivia, current valuations and vessel-specific research were excluded from accepted claims and biographies.
